purpose: Single-axis large steps that separate the horizontal saturation length vxr from the product k = ar*vxr, so the horizontal force ceiling A_r = k/vxr can be stated. Reference: G:/マイドライブ/Experiment/20260919/measurement_plan/NEXT_MEASUREMENTS_20260920.md (item 3) and large_step/make_large_step_trajectory.py (copied to large_step_20260920/).
generation_note: Generated natively by kind=staircase (axis, amplitudes_mm, directions, repeats_within_run), which reproduces the analysis-side commands/vzrstep_*L*.npz exactly (see reference_comparison_20260920.json). Staircase safety is amplitude-only: the offset from the centre, the single-sample change and the 2.144 mm escape boundary. safety_limits are pinned per run just above the designed step.
protocol_note: Escalate: XL12 -> XL15, and only then XL18 -> XL20; the y ladder afterwards if it is still wanted. The simulated ladder keeps the particle at every stage, but 1.8-2.0 mm starts from beyond the estimated force maximum, so watch the return in the preview and stop when it becomes sluggish. Use run_large_step_all.ps1 or --hf-run LABEL=SCALE.

experiments.name: largestep_XL12
experiments.note: Horizontal force ceiling: x only, 0 -> +1.2 -> 0 -> -1.2 -> 0 mm repeated 3 times. 13 holds of 0.4 s (0.5 s at each end), 12 jumps, 5.4 s. A single jump is 1.2 mm = 56% of the estimated 2.144 mm escape boundary; the command never jumps from +1.2 to -1.2. Below 1 mm only the product k = ar*vxr is identifiable, so this ladder separates the saturation length vxr and gives the force ceiling A_r = k/vxr. First step of the ladder; 1.2 mm is close to amplitudes already recorded with the particle retained. Record the ladder from the smallest step upwards and stop where the particle returns sluggishly - that itself is the answer.
